key_insight: Lead-free AgBiS2 memristors can switch at ultra-low voltage and their filament evolution can be tuned from digital to analog by engineering the device interface and thickness.
engineering_relevance: The work points to a sustainable, solution-processable memory platform for neuromorphic hardware with controllable conductance updates and high ON/OFF ratios.
method: First-principles defect and migration calculations to identify native ionic carriers.
Interface and thickness engineering to tune switching from abrupt to gradual.
Electrochemical impedance, pulse tests, and post-operando structural analysis to link dynamics with device behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ~0.08 V SET voltage, ON/OFF ratios above 10^4, and gradual conductance modulation under pulse trains.
watch_item: Repeated filament formation and rupture cause substantial morphological evolution, so long-term durability and variability remain important concerns.
paper_title: Controlling Switching Evolution in Lead-Free Perovskite-Inspired Chalcogenide Memristors for Neuromorphic Computing
